title: My Music Story 🎻 | Slow English Storytime for English Learners
channel: Speak English with Bo's Slow English

lines.text: Hi everyone. My name is Bo, and this is
Bo's Slow English. Today, I want to talk
about music because I realized that
music has been a part of every stage of
my life. I played instruments growing
up, sang in groups, went through
different music phases, and I'm probably
a little opinionated when it comes to
music. I also think music affects people
more than they realize, emotionally and
physically. So, today, I'm going to talk
about some memories I have with music
and how it greatly influenced my life.
Please like, subscribe, and share this
video with your friends. Please also
check out my new YouTube channel. It's
for kids, families, and super beginner
English learners. When I think about my
earliest memories involving music, I
think about my family.
I remember hearing my brother play drums
in the house, and I remember being in
the car listening to whatever music he
liked.
He listened to bands like Dave Matthews
Band,
311, and Metallica.
Looking back now, I realize music was
always around me.
My dad was also a drummer and conducted
an Air Force band, the Korean Air Force
band,
which is kind of interesting because I
don't think I appreciated that growing
up as much as I probably should have.
The reason I started violin was because
one of my aunts in Korea is a violin
teacher and she gifted me a violin.
Buying instruments is expensive, so that
was really my introduction.
I played violin for years in school and
I have mixed feelings when I think back
on it.
Part of me feels proud because I sat
near the front in orchestra at times and
I never took private lessons while many
other students did.
At the same time, I remember comparing
myself to classmates who seemed more
talented or more dedicated.
Looking back, I think comparison took
some enjoyment away.
I probably didn't appreciate my own
ability enough.
I also sang.
I was in choral groups and in elementary
school a cappella group called The
Madrigals.
Actually, one of my early memories is
singing backstage for The Nutcracker
Ballet.
That feels strange to say now because I
don't think people watching my videos
would picture me doing that.
I eventually switched from musicals into
pit orchestra because I wanted to try
something different.
That's a pattern I notice throughout my
life.
I get curious and jump into new things.
I attempted piano,
bass guitar, and I technically know one
song on drums because my brother taught
me. Very basic. I would not call myself
a drummer
or a pianist
or a bass guitarist.
One regret I have is quitting violin
after high school.
I honestly don't even know where my
violin is now.
At the time
playing felt connected to school and
obligations.
So I didn't see it as something
enjoyable.
I wonder sometimes whether I would
appreciate it more now as an adult.
That happens with hobbies sometimes.
You realize later they mattered more
than you thought.
Outside of school
music became something different.
Growing up near Baltimore, I became
interested in underground music scenes.
When I say underground I mean music that
wasn't necessarily popular or played
everywhere.
I listened to punk reggae
techno
house music jazz
hip hop
metal
even Swedish death metal.
Honestly, a little bit of everything

I went through a phase where I liked

which absolutely did not work with my
hair. That was unsuccessful.
Some of the first shows I attended were
with a group of guy friends.
I remember liking the atmosphere.
People cared deeply about music.
It felt less polished and more personal.
I don't know how else to explain it.
Something interesting is that my husband
and I connected partly because of music.
We used to spend time digging for music,
which basically means searching for
artists or songs that weren't well known
and feeling excited when you discovered
something on your own. [clears throat]
For us,
finding music felt almost like a hobby.
I've realized over time that I'm pretty
opinionated
about music. I know this sounds
dramatic, but music can affect my mood a
lot.
For example,
if I'm at the gym

I feel slightly embarrassed admitting
that because it sounds judgmental, but I

Music creates a feeling and a vibe.
I also think music helped me through

whether that was stress, anxiety,

That's one reason I like meditation

Sometimes music feels grounding in a way
